title: MidiSlayer · learn to read music by playing it
excerpt: Plug in a MIDI keyboard and train sight-reading, chords, intervals and scales with live feedback, exam mode and games. Buy once. macOS, Windows, Linux.
content_html:
For pianists learning to read music

Plug in your keyboard and play real pieces. MidiSlayer follows along, shows you every note you got right, and keeps score as you improve.

Free to try. Any MIDI keyboard. macOS, Windows and Linux.

How it works

Playing in about a minute.

Three moves to set up, then MidiSlayer gets out of the way and just listens. No card, no trial clock, no tutorial to sit through.

Step 01

Download it free

MidiSlayer for macOS, Windows or Linux. No card, no trial clock ticking.

Step 02

Plug in your piano

Any USB MIDI keyboard. No keyboard yet? The on-screen one gets you going.

Step 03

Start playing

It follows along and shows you each note as you play it. Missed one? It comes round again until it sticks.

Download for free

Free to start, and the free version never expires. Love it? Unlock the full version whenever you want: one payment, yours to keep, works offline.

See everything inside →

The whole app

See it. Play it. Go again.

Train, Games and Practice: three doors into the same simple loop. Something appears on the staff, you play it on your piano, and you see straight away how you did.

Read the staff

Build the shapes

Own the harmony

Watch yourself improve

See how far you've come.

A few notes today. A little more tomorrow. MidiSlayer remembers every session, note by note, so you can see it all adding up.

The days add up. Your personal bests move up.

See your rank and points grow, with personal bests for every mode.

Note weakness map Slowest notes First-try accuracy Exam score and rank per mode

Your practice data lives on your machine. Optional sync for streaks and bests. No ads. No profiles. No peeking.

Where it's going

It keeps getting better, and the updates are free.

Getting from zero to here took nine modes, three arcade games with a shared daily run of Cascade, Score Practice with a 69-piece library you can play or just listen to, and an analytics suite that measures what you actually retain. That pace didn't stop at launch: the releases below landed since Early Access opened, and updates within v1 are free.

  1. v0.8.0 · 20 Sep · latest

    The Session gets a band

    The Session has a band now. Real drums and a double bass count you in, play a groove (straight, swing, ballad or bossa), listen to how hard you play, and end the tune with you.

  2. v0.7.6 · 18 Sep

    A new look, and steadier under the hood

    A new MidiSlayer mark and wordmark, drawn the Monoglyph way. You will see it in the title bar, on the icon and on midislayer.com.

  3. v0.7.5 · 8 Sep

    Nothing fails quietly any more

    Fixed: if a Grand Piano sample failed to load, the piano stayed silent for the rest of the session with no warning. It now tells you, tries again on your next note, and plays as soon as the load succeeds.

The full notes for every release live in the app, under What's New. It updates itself.

  1. from day one

    Sharpening what ships

    Player feedback, folded in fast from the first build onward. Rough edges filed as they surface, and the loudest requests jump the queue.

  2. shipped · 20 Sep

    The Session, deeper

    A real band of drums and double bass, four grooves, four new tunes to jam over, and a coach that names the note to land on. In the app now, as a free update.

  3. MidiSlayer on iPad

    The full trainer on iPad, where a staff has room to breathe. Phones are a squeeze for sheet music, so tablets lead. Building now, on real hardware.

  4. MidiSlayer on Android

    Then Android tablets too, so nobody is locked out of their own repertoire.

The order is partly yours to call.

We read everything, and the roadmap bends toward what players actually ask for. Buy early, get loud, watch the app grow around you.

Tell us what you need

Questions people ask

Asked and answered.

For the full experience, yes. Any USB MIDI keyboard works, from a $25 controller to a digital grand. No keyboard handy? The built-in on-screen keyboard is enough to try it out. The real thing wants real keys.

macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows 10/11 and Linux (.deb, .rpm and AppImage). Under the hood it's a lean desktop app with a native Rust core: MIDI timing comes off your hardware, your data lives in a local database, and after the one-time licence activation you can practise entirely offline. The app only reaches the network to check your licence, look for updates and, only if you switch it on, sync your progress summary.

Really. One payment and it's yours to keep, with every update through v1 included. No monthly fee, no expiry, nothing to lose access to. A tool you keep, not a treadmill you rent. (Studio seats for schools work differently: those are invoiced per seat once a year.)

A lot. Note Flashcards in full, the Blitz arcade game, a free run of Cascade every day (the Daily Challenge), a jam session over the Pop Loop, the complete course on reading sheet music, and the whole score library to browse and listen to, with four pieces fully playable, one per shelf. Forever, with no card and no trial clock.

Especially for you. MidiSlayer ships with a built-in Learn course that takes you from "what is a staff" to reading your first notes, with real engraved examples, and it's in the free version. Every lesson ends right where the matching training mode begins.

Your key activates on up to two machines at once, any mix of Mac, Windows or Linux. Moving to a new machine is one click of "Deactivate on this device" in Settings. If a dead machine took a slot with it, you can free it yourself from your account page, or email us and we'll do it.

Yes. Activate your licence once and training, games and progress all work without internet, forever. The app only reaches the network to check your licence, to look for updates and, only if you switch it on, to sync your progress summary between your machines. It keeps working when it can't.

On your device, in a local database. No ads, no analytics trackers, and we don't sell your data. Your weak notes are between you and your piano. By default all we hold is your licence: your email, your key, which machines it's on and when each last checked in. If you turn on the optional sync, we also keep a small progress summary (settings, achievements, streaks, best scores) so another machine can pick it up; you can delete it from the app's settings whenever you like.

No. You buy, your key arrives by email, you paste it into the app. If you'd rather manage things yourself there's an optional account at platform.midislayer.com/account: sign in with a link sent to your email (no password) to see your key, check which machines it's on and free a slot. The app never requires sign-in; the one thing an account adds inside the app is the optional progress sync in Settings.

The standard licence is for your own playing, including your own practice as a teacher. Teaching with MidiSlayer, or installing it on your students' machines, is what the Studio plan covers: seats billed once a year on a single invoice, at a rate that drops as you take more. The Studio page has the numbers.

One you'll keep. The address you enter at checkout is paired with your licence key: your key lands there, your account signs in with a link sent there, and support recognises you by it. A work address you might lose is a bad fit. Bought with the wrong one, or moving on from an old address? Contact us and we'll move your licence over.

Purchases and refunds are handled by Paddle, our merchant of record, under Paddle's refund policy. Ask at paddle.net or email us and we'll get it in front of Paddle. The free version exists so you can be sure before you buy.

Something else? Ask us directly. A human reads it, promise.

content_html_zh:
For pianists learning to read music

Plug in your keyboard and play real pieces. MidiSlayer follows along, shows you every note you got right, and keeps score as you improve.

Free to try. Any MIDI keyboard. macOS, Windows and Linux.

它是如何运作的

Playing in about a minute.

Three moves to set up, then MidiSlayer gets out of the way and just listens. No card, no trial clock, no tutorial to sit through.

Step 01

Download it free

MidiSlayer for macOS, Windows or Linux. No card, no trial clock ticking.

Step 02

Plug in your piano

Any USB MIDI keyboard. No keyboard yet? The on-screen one gets you going.

Step 03

Start playing

It follows along and shows you each note as you play it. Missed one? It comes round again until it sticks.

Download for free

Free to start, and the free version never expires. 爱它？ Unlock the full version whenever you want: one payment, yours to keep, works offline.

See everything inside →

The whole app

See it. Play it. Go again.

Train, Games and Practice: three doors into the same simple loop. Something appears on the staff, you play it on your piano, and you see straight away how you did.

Read the staff

Build the shapes

Own the harmony

Watch yourself improve

See how far you've come.

A few notes today. A little more tomorrow. MidiSlayer remembers every session, note by note, so you can see it all adding up.

The days add up. Your personal bests move up.

See your rank and points grow, with personal bests for every mode.

Note weakness map Slowest notes First-try accuracy Exam score and rank per mode

Your practice data lives on your machine. Optional sync for streaks and bests. 没有广告。 No profiles. No peeking.

Where it's going

It keeps getting better, and the updates are free.

Getting from zero to here took nine modes, three arcade games with a shared daily run of Cascade, Score Practice with a 69-piece library you can play or just listen to, and an analytics suite that measures what you actually retain. That pace didn't stop at launch: the releases below landed since Early Access opened, and updates within v1 are free.

  1. v0.8.0 · 20 Sep · latestThe Session gets a bandThe Session has a band now. Real drums and a double bass count you in, play a groove (straight, swing, ballad or bossa), listen to how hard you play, and end the tune with you.
  2. v0.7.6 · 18 SepA new look, and steadier under the hoodA new MidiSlayer mark and wordmark, drawn the Monoglyph way. You will see it in the title bar, on the icon and on midislayer.com.
  3. v0.7.5 · 8 SepNothing fails quietly any moreFixed: if a Grand Piano sample failed to load, the piano stayed silent for the rest of the session with no warning. It now tells you, tries again on your next note, and plays as soon as the load succeeds.

The full notes for every release live in the app, under What's New. It updates itself.

  1. from day oneSharpening what shipsPlayer feedback, folded in fast from the first build onward. Rough edges filed as they surface, and the loudest requests jump the queue.
  2. shipped · 20 SepThe Session, deeperA real band of drums and double bass, four grooves, four new tunes to jam over, and a coach that names the note to land on. In the app now, as a free update.
  3. MidiSlayer on iPadThe full trainer on iPad, where a staff has room to breathe. Phones are a squeeze for sheet music, so tablets lead. Building now, on real hardware.
  4. MidiSlayer on AndroidThen Android tablets too, so nobody is locked out of their own repertoire.

The order is partly yours to call.

We read everything, and the roadmap bends toward what players actually ask for. Buy early, get loud, watch the app grow around you.
